claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi programs.
The Pulumi Terraform provider exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments and references a Terraform state file stored in S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` objects have a `getOutput(name)` method that returns outputs from the referenced Terraform state.
The `terraform.state.S3Reference` class is accessible as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` via the `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` import (aliased as `pulumi`).
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` and `getOutput("vpcId")` are the way to reference outputs from another Pulumi stack.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties, where logging can be set to "DEFAULT".
The `pulumi import` command can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The `pulumi import` command syntax is `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
A Pulumi program can call a 'Pulumi import API' to import resources programmatically, as suggested by the migration helper class.
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policies use `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and `validateResource` with a callback (instance, args, reportViolation).
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be "public-read" or "public-read-write".
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Automation API exposes `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` taking `stackName`, `projectName`, and an inline `program`, plus `stack.setConfig(key, {value})` and `stack.up({onOutput})` returning a result with `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving multi-tool management complexity to the platform team rather than development teams.
The `@pulumi/terraform` package exists and exports the `terraform.state.S3Reference` type.
Custom component resources are created by extending `pulumi.ComponentResource` and calling `super(type, name, {}, opts)` in the constructor, then `registerOutputs`.

The `aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` (with `requiresCompatibilities`, `networkMode`, `cpu`, `memory`, `containerDefinitions`) and `aws.ecs.Service` (with `launchType`, `networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp`) resources accept the arguments shown.
